**Region Sjælland** (the administrative organization) and **Sjælland** (the geographical region label used in statistical breakdowns) represent one of Denmark's five regions within the [[adhd-databasen|ADHD-DATABASEN]]. In the context of national ADHD diagnostic and treatment quality reports, the two terms are used interchangeably to track the region's clinical performance, patient volumes, and adherence to national healthcare indicators. 

Region Sjælland is notable for its fluctuating patient volumes and diagnostic pathways. According to the 2023 report, the region experienced a 24% increase in the number of diagnostic pathways, a surge it shared with [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], which served as a comparative baseline against the declining numbers seen in [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] [^src1]. The region's specific departments, such as [[boerne-unge-psyk-afd-40|Børne-Unge Psyk. Afd. 40]], contribute directly to these regional datasets [^src2]. Furthermore, there are significant regional differences in how heavily the region relies on specific pathway markers like [[agx01b|AGX01B]] [^src6].

When evaluating clinical quality, Sjælland shows mixed and sometimes unstable results across various indicators. For [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]], the region's performance sits close to the national average but has experienced notable shifts, dropping to 49% in the 2024/25 reporting period [^src7]. The region faces particular challenges with early childhood and adolescent diagnostic timelines. For [[indikator-2a|Indikator 2a]], which measures clinical environment observations for children aged 0-5 within 120 days, Region Sjælland recorded the lowest national performance at just 17% [^src8], with specific fulfillment rates around 23% in 2023/24 [^src2]. Similarly, for [[indikator-2b|Indikator 2b]] (diagnostic interviews or observations for 6-17-year-olds), the region demonstrated significant variation, achieving only 32% compared to 70% in [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] [^src14], and a 31% target fulfillment in the prior year [^src3]. 

For other clinical metrics, Sjælland's results reflect broader national struggles and regional disparities. Both Sjælland and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] reached a 50% fulfillment rate for [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] [^src9]. For [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], the region scored 49%, sitting just below the national top performer [^src10]. In metrics with lower overall compliance, such as [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]], Sjælland and [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] reported 0% among regions with a minimum of three patients [^src15], and like all other regions, it failed to collectively fulfill [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] [^src11]. However, the region showed stronger performance on [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]], achieving an 81% rate [^src12]. 

Ultimately, the data for Region Sjælland highlights a healthcare area with increasing diagnostic volumes but inconsistent quality development, emphasizing the need for targeted improvements in pediatric ADHD assessments.
